newsitem.title: UK: Mobius says Thai stocks oversold, sees bounce.
newsitem.headline: Mobius says Thai stocks oversold, sees bounce.

text.p: Emerging markets guru Mark Mobius said on Friday his Templeton Emerging Markets Investment Trust had made significant purchases in Thailand in the belief that the stockmarket's fall has been overdone.
"We believe that the decline in the market has been overdone and that reports of the poor condition of the Thai economy have been overstated," Mobius said in a review of the trust's annual results.

He said the Thai stockmarket has fallen some 65 percent since December 1994, with many well managed company shares now selling for as little as three times earnings, and the market average at nine times earnings.
"Many bargains are available in the market at the present time and we believe that the upside potential for the market is very real."
Mobius said his 727.7 million sterling trust's biggest purchase of the year to April 30 had been a $30 million investment in Thailand.
Other big purchases in the year included $20 million in Mexico, $18 million in India, $17 million in Korea and $16 million in South Africa.
The trust's biggest holding at end-April was Brazil, accounting for 16.1 percent of the fund. It replaced Hong Kong, which was the top market until Templeton took profits there.
The trust's net asset value rose 12.2 percent in the year, compared with the benchmark IFCI Composite Index which was down 2.6 percent and the MSCI World Index, which was up 2.5 percent.
